## Current behavior So it looks like between 5.1.x and 5.2.x something has changed with the injector. Maybe related? #938 #977 ### Before ``` [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/:user_id, GET} route +1ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/:user_id, PUT} route +0ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/:user_id, DELETE} route +0ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RoutesResolver] MfaController {/mfa}: +1ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/system-info, POST} route +0ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/user-info, POST} route +1ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/create-user, POST} route +0ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/update-user-info, POST} route +0ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/enroll, POST} route +1ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/unenroll, POST} route +0ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/analyze, POST} route +0ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/challenge, POST} route +1ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/authenticate, POST} route +0ms [Nest] 66564 - 2018-8-23 14:31:02 [RouterExplorer] Mapped {/create-support-incident, POST} route +0ms ``` ### After ``` [Nest] 67506 - 2018-8-23 14:33:17 [NestFactory] Starting Nest application... [Nest] 67506 - 2018-8-23 14:33:17 [InstanceLoader] MongooseModule dependencies initialized +35ms [Nest] 67506 - 2018-8-23 14:33:17 [InstanceLoader] RequestModule dependencies initialized +0ms [Nest] 67506 - 2018-8-23 14:33:17 [ExceptionHandler] Nest can't resolve dependencies of the MfaService (?, MfaCallbackConfig). Please make sure that the argument at index [0] is available in the current context. +2ms Error: Nest can't resolve dependencies of the MfaService (?, MfaCallbackConfig). Please make sure that the argument at index [0] is available in the current context. at Injector.lookupComponentInExports (/Users/cain/git/some/project/node_modules/@nestjs/core/injector/injector.js:146:19) at at process._tickDomainCallback (internal/process/next_tick.js:228:7) 1: node::Abort() [/Users/cain/.nvm/versions/node/v8.11.4/bin/node] 2: node::Chdir(v8::FunctionCallbackInfo const&) [/Users/cain/.nvm/versions/node/v8.11.4/bin/node] 3: v8::internal [/Users/cain/.nvm/versions/node/v8.11.4/bin/node] 4: 70% building modules 876/876 modules 0 activev8::internal::MaybeHandle v8::internal::(anonymous namespace)::HandleApiCallHelper(v8::internal::Isolate*, v8::internal::Handle, v8::internal::Handle, v8::internal::Handle, v8::internal::Handle, v8::internal::BuiltinArguments) [/Users/cain/.nvm/versions/node/v8.11.4/bin/node] 70% finish module graph FlagDependencyExportsPluginv8::internal::Builtin_Impl_HandleApiCall(v8::internal::BuiltinArguments, v8::internal::Isolate*) [/Users/cain/.nvm/versions/node/v8.11.4/bin/node] 6: 0x2f644d2042fd ``` ## Expected behavior Should be able to dynamically configure module and have DI work as expected. ## Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions I have a simple module which has configuration to create a `DynamicModule`: ```typescript const IMPORT_EXPORT = [MfaService]; const DEFAULT_CONFIG: Partial = { // redacted }; @Module({ imports: IMPORT_EXPORT, exports: IMPORT_EXPORT, providers: [], controllers: [MfaController], }) export class MfaModule { static forRoot(config: MfaModuleConfig, callbackConfig: MfaCallbackConfig = {}): DynamicModule { const providers= [ MfaService, { provide: 'MfaModuleConfig', useValue: { ...DEFAULT_CONFIG, ...config, } }, { provide: 'MfaCallbackConfig', useValue: callbackConfig, } ]; return { module: MfaModule, providers, } } } ``` Which I am importing into my module like so: ```typescript MfaModule.forRoot({ host: process.env.MFA_HOST || 'host', key: process.env.MFA_API_KEY || 'api-key', }), ``` My service has something as follows: ```typescript export class MfaService { mfaApi: MfaApi; mfaController: MfaController; constructor( @Inject('MfaModuleConfig') public mfaModuleConfig: MfaModuleConfig, @Inject('MfaCallbackConfig') public callbackConfig: MfaCallbackConfig ) { ``` I am not using `MfaService` anywhere else except within the `MfaModule` at this point, so I am not sure how this is possible. I also have this MfaModule as a library that I am importing into this project. I have the intent to share this module with other projects. I have checked that there is only one instance of @nestjs in my node_modules to ensure that DI is working correctly. I have a separate module built out very much in the same way and is importing fine, so I'm not quite sure what the reproduction is. I will try to see if I can come up with a concrete reproduction. ## What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior? Trying to create 3rd party modules to be consumed by nestjs backends. ## Environment 

Nest version: 5.2.1

 
For Tooling issues:
- Node version: v8.11.4  
- Platform: Mac 

Others:
## PS Love the work that you are doing here and thanks for such a great backend framework!

items.title: Regression: Additional GRPC options can't be set anymore in Nestjs 7
items.body:
## Bug Report

## Original behavior in Nestjs 6
In Nestjs 6, it was possible to set all GRPC options, e.g. grpc.ssl_target_name_override and grpc.default_authority which are required to have GRPC-SSL enabled on localhost:

```
const grpcOptionsAny: any = grpcClientOptions.options;
grpcOptionsAny['grpc.ssl_target_name_override'] = 'localhost';
grpcOptionsAny['grpc.default_authority'] = 'localhost';
```

## Breaking change
The commit 0b38029830f59d8a0092137c39ea4b30aa1377cb changed this behavior by removing `...this.options` from the used option-Object:

https://github.com/nestjs/nest/commit/0b38029830f59d8a0092137c39ea4b30aa1377cb#r38494866

Now, most of the GRPC-options are unavailable when using Nestjs:
https://grpc.github.io/grpc/core/group__grpc__arg__keys.html
